title: Circles: Tangents to a Circle
seo_title: Circles Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 10)
standard_text: Tangent to a circle at the point of contact; the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact; the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Circles worksheet (NCERT Chapter 10): tangents and secants, tangent ⟂ radius, equal tangents from an external point, circumscribed quadrilaterals and concentric circles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Tangent ⟂ radius at the point of contact
key_sub: Tangents from an external point are equal.
body_html:
How it works

A tangent meets a circle at exactly one point, the point of contact. A secant meets it at two points.

Theorem 10.1: the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. So tangent length = √(OT² − r²).

Theorem 10.2: the tangents from an external point are equal. The line from the external point to the centre bisects the angle between them, and ∠APB + ∠AOB = 180°.

Example

From Q, the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and OQ = 25 cm. Find the radius.

Radius ⟂ tangent

r = √(25² − 24²) = √49

Answer: 7 cm

Example

ABCD circumscribes a circle. AB = 6, BC = 7, CD = 4. Find AD.

AB + CD = AD + BC

10 = AD + 7

Answer: AD = 3 cm

Common mistakes

  • Taking OT − r as the tangent length. Use Pythagoras: √(OT² − r²).
  • Writing ∠AOB = ∠APB. They are supplementary: they add up to 180°.
  • Using AB + BC = CD + DA for a circumscribed quadrilateral. The opposite sides add up: AB + CD = AD + BC.

faq.q: What is a tangent to a circle?
faq.a: A line that meets the circle at exactly one point. That point is called the point of contact.

faq.q: Why is the tangent perpendicular to the radius?
faq.a: The point of contact is the only point of the tangent on the circle; every other point is outside, so OP is the shortest distance from O to the line, and the shortest distance is the perpendicular.

faq.q: How many tangents can be drawn from a point outside a circle?
faq.a: Exactly two, and they are equal in length.

faq.q: What is true for a quadrilateral that circumscribes a circle?
faq.a: The sums of opposite sides are equal: AB + CD = AD + BC.

items.q: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 8 cm and the distance of Q from the centre is 10 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
items.e: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent: r = √(10² − 8²) = 6 cm.

items.q: A line that meets a circle at exactly one point is called a ___.
items.e: A tangent touches the circle at one point (the point of contact). tangent.

items.q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point on the circle?
items.e: At a point on the circle there is exactly one tangent. One.

items.q: The tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are ___.
items.e: Both are perpendicular to the same diameter, so they are parallel. parallel.

items.q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point outside it?
items.e: From an external point there are exactly two tangents. Two.

items.q: A tangent PQ is drawn at the point P of a circle with centre O and radius 9 cm. A point Q on the tangent is 41 cm from O. Find PQ.
items.e: OP ⟂ PQ, so PQ = √(OQ² − OP²) = √(41² − 9²) = 40 cm.

items.q: TA and TB are tangents from T to a circle with centre O and radius 7 cm. TA = 24 cm. Find the area of the kite OATB.
items.e: Triangles OAT and OBT are congruent right-angled triangles, each with area ½ × 7 × 24. Kite area = 2 × ½ × 7 × 24 = 168 cm².

items.q: Two concentric circles have radii 50 cm and 14 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle.
items.e: The chord is a tangent to the smaller circle, so it is perpendicular to the radius and bisected: half chord = √(50² − 14²) = 48 cm. Chord = 96 cm.
